quote: then set $D_\tau\leftarrow D_\tau-H_\sigma$
note: After D<-D+H the pair is (eta, zeta+eta); after the swap it is (zeta+eta, eta); then D<-D-H gives eta-(zeta+eta) = -zeta, so the pair is (eta+zeta, -zeta), not (eta+zeta, zeta) as claimed. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, line ~1436) uses D_j <- H_i - D_j, which gives zeta. The last step should be D_tau <- H_sigma - D_tau.

note: The bit network, its wires, edges and the matrix on each edge are never defined on this page; the linked page covers only generic networks with roles and frames.

note: Wrong and does not follow. The telescoping holds for any intermediate frames, so it cannot force them to be the identity. Only the scalar gates of the bit network are over F_2. In an odd-characteristic residue ring subtraction and addition do not coincide, so the three updates D-H, H+D, H-D are genuine modular additions and subtractions, not XORs. The page also states the shear is 'over $\mathbb F_2$', which the paper does not.

quote: By the telescoping, the route applies $\varepsilon_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$
note: The result needs the supplied physical input f to be read as the logical array D_in^{-1} f (the paper, lines 141-142 and 794-805, defines this); the page never says how the input is interpreted, so the factor D_source(w)^{-1} appears without justification.

quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
note: The page never says what nondegenerate means for a subspace, nor that F carries the tensor-product bilinear form, nor what U^perp means (it is orthogonal complement under that form, not the dot product). The projection P_U along U^perp and the dimensions D-1 of U^perp exist only because the lines are nondegenerate (self-pairing 2^3, nonzero), which the page does not state.

note: Overstated: the geometric series converges (ratio below 1) only when lambda>log_m(s/W), and the page also needs lambda>tau(1+eta/vartheta) and lambda<1. For small lambda the ratio exceeds 1 and the sum is not O(f^lambda). The paper (line 2416) uses a<m^lambda, i.e. only lambda in the stated range.

quote: The outer two take linear time.
note: The page does not say why D<-D-H and D<-H-D cost only linear time. The reason (paper Section on tape interchange) is that they update the later field using the earlier field in tape order, which a single scan can do; the reader is not given this and cannot check it.

quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
note: No recurrence is given or linked on this page, and the reader is not told how fewer than R interchanges per wire yields a power saving. This is left entirely unexplained.

quote: gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The reader is not told what a negative source projection, a decreasing edge or the dimension lost on one is, nor what the rank budget counts, so the identity and the inequality N>2L_b cannot be interpreted. quote: The outer two cost linear time.
note: The page gives no reason why D<-D-H and D<-H-D, with H and D multi-bit fields on tape, take linear time. The paper (line 1540) says these update the later field from the earlier one and cites its ordered-affine-streams lemma; the page neither states nor links this.

note: False and inconsistent with the page: the page itself says the construction gives s<Wm, i.e. s/W<m, and the next sentence needs log_m(s/W)<1. The saving exists because s/W<m (paper lines 168, 1468, 2239). The inequality is reversed.

quote: a forward invocation from $X$ to $Y$ subtracts $x_S$ from $y_S$ and changes no other value (cited)
note: The paper's Lemma (lines 729-730) says a forward invocation changes y_S to y_S+x_S, i.e. it adds x_S to y_S; the inverse schedule is the one that subtracts. Subtracting also contradicts the page's next sentence, since the shear H<-H+D adds D to H.

quote: distinct triples are orthogonal
note: False as stated. The form gives <t_T,t_S>=|T cap S|-1, which is zero only when |T cap S|=1, i.e. for neighbors; triples meeting in 0 or 2 elements give -1 or 1. The paper (line ~869) says only that neighboring triple lines are orthogonal.

quote: each losing $h$ on a decreasing edge
note: The page never gives the gate labels, their time order, or the decomposition into B, P, A that shows central wires lose exactly h once and no other edge decreases, so L=3 binom(h,3)^2 h^2 cannot be checked.

quote: Sources have dimension $1$, summing to $N$; sinks have dimension $D$, except the $N$ sinks that receive the sources, which have label $U_\iota^\perp$ and dimension $D-1$.
note: The page never states the terminal labels (source label U_iota for the source of index iota, zero for others; sink label the whole space, except U_iota^perp for the sinks receiving the sources, and which roles those are), nor that the wire count W counts all roles, so the reader cannot check these dimension sums.

quote: gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The identity and the inequality N>2L_b are only cited; the page does not say what edge matrices are or why their ranks equal the dimension changes (paper lines 1148-1167), so the reader cannot check that s_b<W_bR.

quote: never removed from $A_{ST}$ afterwards (no undo-copy step)
note: False. The paper's schedule (lines 700-730, eq. motif-schedule) has row 6 'undo gather' and row 7 'undo copy', and also rows 0 and 1 that subtract the effect of old scratch values; the construction restores every auxiliary value and works for arbitrary initial scratch values (Lemma scalar-motifs). The page's description, with copies left on A_ST, leaves the auxiliary wires changed and contradicts the page's own 'fixed network ... makes few enough smaller calls' with restored scratch.

quote: A field of $u=m^k$ bits therefore has $Q_k=O(u^\tau)$, and the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$.
note: Missing hypotheses. The paper's Proposition power-interchange (lines 1475-1487) covers only widths e=m^k radix-q digits and requires a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k (needed to split rows evenly into W role streams of volume V/W at each of k levels); the page's recurrence silently assumes this. The O(Vu^tau) bound for arbitrary u needs Lemma chunk-swap (line 1631): padding rows, writing the width in base m and interchanging pieces. The page proves only the u=m^k case under the unstated row condition yet states the general cost.

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
note: The page never says what a kernel is (in the paper, the 2-input butterfly-like C map applied individually on one selected bit/chunk, costing O(V) each). The reader has no way to see why f/m^nu chunks cost O(f/m^nu) per unit volume.

quote: Any invertible linear transformation of $H$ or $D$ costs $O(V)$ (cited)
note: Stated too widely. Only lower-triangular invertible transformations cost O(V), because they update coordinates from last to first using earlier unchanged coordinates (the page's own justification). A general invertible matrix has no such order. Paper, Lemma matrix-shear proof (line 1425): 'A lower triangular transformation of H, or of D, costs O(V)'.

quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
note: The page never explains what a source, gate, sink, edge or route of the network is (wires, gates touching them in time order, consecutive vertices joined by edges), nor how two banks are exchanged. A reader of this background cannot tell what the nodes and edges are.

quote: Each role stream then holds $V/(2W)$ bits (cited).
note: Wrong constant. V bits are split evenly among W roles, so each role stream holds V/W bits (paper line 127 and line 1544, volume V/W), not V/(2W).

quote: on arrays indexed by the common address set
note: The page never defines the common address set: that each role stream (V/W bits) has the same local address set, so arrays on different wires can be combined pointwise and one frame can act on them. The reader cannot tell what the frames act on.

quote: which for width $u=\mu^d$ is $O(u^{\tau})$ per unit volume
note: The recursion splits into W role streams at every level, which needs a row field divisible by W^d (paper line 1483, Proposition power-interchange). The page omits this hypothesis; the paper reaches arbitrary widths and shapes only after padding rows (Lemma at line 1631). As stated, the recursion for width mu^d is claimed for any array.

quote: Each unit of rank costs one smaller call.
note: Cited with no explanation of why: the page never says what a smaller call is, how an edge's matrix change is carried out on arrays of tape data (the shear/interchange of address fields), or why a rank-r matrix difference costs r calls. This is the link that turns the rank sum s into the recursion's cost, and is the page's own concept, so a citation does not make it followable.

quote: For the bit network, $s<W$ (cited)
note: The paper's bit network satisfies s_b < W_b m (Proposition bit-motif-interface, paper line 1148 to 1151; contract s<Wm at line 1468; intro line 168), not s<W. The page itself then says s is Wm minus a positive constant and concludes s/W<m, and later treats the case s/W>1, all of which contradict s<W (which would force s/W<1). The correct cited statement is s<Wm.

The page never gives the size of the explicit network's matrices and does not cite where mu<2^20 comes from (the paper has m=h^3=10^6 at line 656, and uses it at line 1332). The reader cannot check this bound, which the exponent choice depends on.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: Does not follow from the preceding sentence, which only requires q not to divide the denominators xi. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, around line 1417) requires a fixed odd prime avoiding every denominator in the table of factorizations and the numerators of diagonal entries of the invertible factors; avoiding all numerators and denominators is only a sufficient example choice. The page also never says which finite collection of matrices is meant or why such a q exists, so the reader cannot see why q can be fixed independent of b.

quote: which may be taken to be $2$
note: Wrong. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, line 1396-1397) requires a fixed ODD prime q, and the bit network's edge matrix 2P_{U_a} (line 1164) has numerator 2, so q=2 would divide a numerator and the factors would not stay invertible mod q. q must avoid all denominators and diagonal numerators of the matrices, so it cannot be taken to be 2.

quote: Since $m^\tau\to m$ as $\tau\to1$, fix $\tau<1$ with $s/W>m^\tau$.
note: Wrong inequality direction. The preceding sentence gives s/W<m, so one can fix tau<1 with s/W<m^tau (paper line 1481: 'Choose a rational number tau in (0,1) with s/W<m^tau'). The page itself later uses 'because $s/W<m^\tau$', so s/W>m^tau contradicts it, and with s/W>m^tau the recurrence would give a bound larger than O(m^{k tau}).

quote: each losing $h$ on a decreasing edge
note: Which edges decrease and why each central wire loses exactly h dimensions depends on the paper's gate-label table (lines 971-990) and the residual table (lines 1010-1035), neither of which the page gives. The reader cannot check that no other edge decreases, so L=3 binom(h,3)^2 h^2 is asserted without support.

quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
note: No recurrence is stated on this page, and chunk width and the recursion in which the interchanges are called recursively are not defined, so the reader cannot see how fewer than R interchanges per wire gives a power saving.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: Does not follow from the previous sentence, which only requires q not to divide denominators. Also false as stated, since a zero entry has numerator 0, which q divides. The paper (lines 1411-1413) requires q to avoid every denominator and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so that the triangular factors stay invertible mod q; the page never gives this reason.

quote: A label $U$ is a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F$.
note: The page never says what nondegenerate means for a subspace relative to the bilinear form (form restricted to U is nondegenerate, so U and U^perp split the space); the reader needs this for P_U to exist.

quote: each losing $h$ on a decreasing edge
note: The page never gives the gate labels or the schedule, so the reader cannot check that the only decreasing edges are one per central wire and each loses exactly h (the paper shows this in its label table and Lemma on residuals, lines 1006-1070). Without it, L and the whole count s are unsupported.

The paper has m=h^3=1000000 (line 656), which is greater than 2^19=524288, so mu<2^19 is false. The paper (line 1332) states m<2^20 (with log 2<1, so log m<20). The conclusion ln mu<20 still holds, but the stated premise is wrong; correct is mu<2^20.

quote: So the shear needs $2\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
note: Each update uses one interchange (the page says so just before), and there are rank_Q M ones in Pi, so the shear needs rank_Q M interchanges, not twice that. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, lines ~1394-1441) says exactly a interchanges for rank a, and 'It uses just one interchange'. The factor 2 contradicts the page's own count and the later claim that s_b is the sum of the ranks.

quote: Unrolling gives $Q_k\le (s/W)^k Q_0-C\sum_{j<k}(s/W)^j$.
note: Sign error. From Q_k <= (s/W)Q_{k-1} + C the unrolled bound is Q_k <= (s/W)^k Q_0 + C sum_{j<k}(s/W)^j, with a plus. With a minus the bound does not follow and the next sentence (the sum is a cost term to be bounded) would be pointless. Paper recurrence (eq:swap-recurrence, line ~1551): F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1), then the geometric sum is added.

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
note: The page never says what a kernel is (the paper's individual selected-bit C kernel applied to one chunk), nor why one kernel costs O(1) per chunk per unit volume, so the reader cannot check the leaf cost.

quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
note: X, Y are banks of scalars indexed by triples, while H, D are address fields of an array. The page never says how the address shear on role streams is a forward invocation, or why exactness for scratch wires gives exactness for scratch rows. The paper gets this from the frame identity and the row split (lines 1520-1532), not by identifying the shear with an invocation.

quote: A level-$k$ call makes $s$ calls at level $k-1$, each on volume $V/W$
note: The page never says that a width m^k field is split into m subfields of width m^(k-1) (vectors H, D of m entries), nor that each unit of rank of an edge matrix costs one interchange of such subfields. Without that construction (paper.tex lines 1495-1497, 1506-1510) the reader cannot see why the sub-calls are at level k-1.

quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set
note: The page never says what sources, sinks, nodes, edges and routes of the network are (the paper: the vertices on a wire are its source, the gates touching it in time order, and its sink; edges join consecutive vertices), nor what the common address set is. The reader has no picture of the graph the frames are attached to.

quote: $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: Not justified and in general false. The computation gives only O(f^sigma u^{1-sigma}) <= O(f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)}); this is <= f^lambda only if f >= d^{vartheta(1-sigma)/(lambda-sigma)}, which is much larger than the internal-node threshold f >= d^vartheta (at f about d^vartheta it exceeds f^lambda). The paper (lines 2420-2430) stops at O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and keeps it as a separate term, d^{sigma+beta(1-sigma)}, in the final bound with the larger exponent lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)} (lines 2440-2450), so the page's conclusion is stronger than the paper's.

quote: multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign
note: Wrong sign. The route multiplies by eps_w in {+1,-1}; removing it means multiplying by eps_w again (eps_w^2=1), as the paper does ('Negate those outputs' only where the sign is -1, paper lines 146 and 1312). Multiplying by -eps_w would leave the factor -1 on every role, and would flip scratch roles (sign +1), contradicting the next sentence that scratch needs no correction.

quote: For any labels $U,V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on $U\oplus V^\perp$, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$.
note: Missing hypothesis: this holds only when U is contained in V (paper line 1158, 'For $U\subset V$ nondegenerate'). For arbitrary labels P_V-P_U need not be the identity on V∩U^perp, nor have rank dim V - dim U (e.g. two different lines U,V give rank 1 or 2 but dim V - dim U = 0). Correct: for U ⊂ V; reversing the edge negates the matrix, rank unchanged.

quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The formula is asserted with no derivation or statement of why it holds. Negative source projections and decreasing edges are never explained, so the reader cannot check the formula or see why s_b is the sum of edge ranks.

The paper (line 1331) states both deficits are greater than 20*2^{-50}, not 20*2^{-40}. With 2^{-40} the claim is stronger than the paper and false: eta_b = 339/22587335000000 is about 1.5e-11, while 20*2^{-40} is about 1.8e-11. The later step 1-20*2^{-50} > 1-eta also only needs 2^{-50}.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: Not true in general: leaves have f/m^nu < d^vartheta, and at f near d^vartheta the quantity f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is about f, which exceeds f^lambda. The paper (around lines 2400-2420) only gets O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and carries it into the final bound d^{sigma+beta(1-sigma)} (hence lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}), not O(e^lambda).

quote: each losing $h$ on a decreasing edge
note: The page never says which edges decrease, why only the central wires do, or why each loses exactly h. In the paper (Lemma lem:motif-residuals, around lines 1000-1070) the only decreasing edge is the central-wire edge from time 3 to 4, losing P tensor F of dimension h, which rests on the stage labels and gate schedule the page does not give.

quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation; after the first update $D$ holds the XOR of $D$ and $H$.
note: The address updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D are over Z/q^b Z with q an odd prime (paper lines 1404 to 1406, 1535 to 1541), where they are not XORs. What is pointwise XOR in the paper are the bit gates of the network (line 1139) acting on the data; the XOR combinations of intermediate data arise from that, not from the address updates being over F_2.

note: Gates combine several wires, so a single route with a sign is not defined for an arbitrary network. It holds only because the scalar network as a whole is a signed permutation of roles; the paper (lines 816-823) derives the route formula from the whole-network identity D_out S D_in^{-1}, which the page never states. The page does not say the scalar network is a signed role permutation.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: The page does not say what bound is stated, nor how s<WD yields it, so a cited result is left with no content or role. It should state the property (the rank sum s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m, with each unit of rank costing one smaller interchange, paper line 1139).

quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges, gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The reader is not told what the bit network's wires, edges, 'negative source projections' or 'dimension lost on decreasing edges' are, nor why each edge's rank equals its dimension change except at the N exceptional edges. The cited claim stands in for how the page's own count of interchanges works and its content cannot be checked from the page.

quote: if a route has source frame $I$ and sink frame $D_\nu$, its operator is $D_\nu$
note: Inconsistent with the page's own formula: a route applies epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, so with source frame I and sink frame D_nu the route operator is epsilon_w D_nu. It equals D_nu only after the sign is undone, i.e. the endpoint operator (paper lines 819-822).

quote: The outer two cost linear time.
note: The page never says that field D comes after H in tape order. The linear-time claim holds only because the outer updates change the later field using the earlier one (paper.tex lines 1347-1352 and 1520-1523, 'The other two updates target the later group'; Lemma matrix-shear needs every H_i before every D_j). Without this hypothesis the claim is unsupported.

quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
note: The banks X, Y are sets of wire roles whose scalars are combined by gates. H and D are address fields of the array. In the paper the shear H<-H+D arises from the frame identity (sink minus source matrix equals the identity, lines 1495-1520) applied to every role stream, not by identifying D with X and H with Y. The page also blends the exchange of banks (X,Y) by the forward, inverse, forward schedule with the exchange of fields H, D done by the three updates, and gives no argument for the identification.

quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
note: The page never explains the network's structure: that each wire has a source, then the gates touching it in time order, then a sink, with edges joining consecutive vertices (paper lines 660-668), nor what 'two banks' of exchanged values are. Source, sink, node, edge and route are used without definition.

quote: for the bit procedure this ring is $\mathbb F_2$, where subtraction and addition coincide
note: Misstates the ring. In the paper (Lemma matrix-shear, lines ~1396-1405, and Proposition power-interchange, line ~1494) the fields H, D range over [q^b] and the shear and the three updates are over Z/q^b Z for a fixed odd prime q chosen to avoid denominators of the rational matrices. Over an odd modulus subtraction and addition do not coincide, so the three updates D-H, H+D, H-D do not collapse to XORs of the address fields. XOR is only the gate applied pointwise to the stored bits of the role streams. The later claim that 'each update is a pointwise XOR' on the fields is therefore not what the paper states.

quote: A field of $u=m^k$ bits therefore has $Q_k=O(u^\tau)$, and the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$.
note: Missing hypotheses. The paper's Proposition power-interchange (lines 1476-1487) requires width exactly a power m^k and a row field before both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k. The recursion needs enough rows to split into W role streams at every level. The page omits the row condition. Arbitrary widths u need a separate lemma (Lemma chunk-swap, line 1632) with padding, not this recurrence.

quote: for the bit procedure this ring is $\mathbb F_2$, where subtraction and addition coincide.
note: Wrong. In the paper (Lemma matrix-shear, about line 1395, and the frame paragraph near line 1129) the address fields range over [q^b] with arithmetic in Z/q^b Z for a fixed ODD prime q; only the map on array entries is F_2-linear. Over an odd modulus subtraction and addition do not coincide, so the three updates D-H, H+D, H-D are genuinely different and the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) is over Z/q^b Z, not F_2 (same error in 'the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$ over $\mathbb F_2$'). The page's F_2 example hides this.

quote: $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: Does not follow. The leaf bound f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is not at most f^lambda: since only sigma<lambda is assumed and f can be as large as d, it is d^{sigma+vartheta(1-sigma)}, which can exceed d^lambda (e.g. vartheta=1/2, sigma=0.79, lambda=0.8 gives 0.895>0.8). The paper (lines 2425-2426, 2437-2445) keeps the leaf term as O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and absorbs it only in the final bound O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda' > max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}.

quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation
note: The three updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D are address permutations over Z/q^b Z with q an odd prime (paper.tex lines 1395-1404, 1425-1445, 1535-1545), not pointwise XORs of F_2 vectors. Only the gates of the network on the data bits are XORs (Proposition bit-motif-interface, line 1139). The page conflates the two.

quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\lambda<\log_m(s/W)<1$ makes the ratio below 1
note: The ratio (s/W)/m^lambda is below 1 exactly when lambda > log_m(s/W), not <. The paper uses a<=m^sigma<m^lambda (a=s/W) with lambda>sigma>=log_m(s/W). The page's own example (lambda=0.8 > 0.585) and its later 'sigma < lambda' with sigma >= log_m(s/W) use the correct direction.

quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
note: Here u counts chunks, whereas earlier on the same page u is a number of bits of a field (u = f Omega bits) and it is the field width of the address-fields page. The page flags other letter changes but not this one, so the reader cannot tell the two uses apart.

quote: =D_{\alpha_k}D_{\alpha_1}^{-1}
note: Wrong. In the product (D_{a_k}D_{a_{k-1}}^{-1})...(D_{a_1}D_{a_0}^{-1}) everything cancels except D_{a_k} on the left and D_{a_0}^{-1} on the right, so the result is D_{a_k}D_{a_0}^{-1}, not D_{a_k}D_{a_1}^{-1}. The page's own next paragraph uses the source frame D_source(w)^{-1} (the first node), and the paper (lines 143-145) has sink and source endpoints.

quote: so $2L>N$ and $s<WD$
note: Wrong inequality direction. L/N=100/539<1/2, so 2L<N, and that is exactly what gives s=WD-N+2L<WD. With 2L>N one would get s>WD. The paper (line ~1110) says both loss ratios are smaller than 1/2.

quote: the paper's proof computes $s$ as $Wm/2$ minus a positive constant fixed by the construction
note: Wrong value. The paper (Proposition bit-motif-interface, lines ~1148-1152) has s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b, with deficit N - 2L_b > 0 from W_b m, so s is Wm minus a positive constant, not Wm/2 minus a constant. The relative deficit is tiny (eta_b = 339/22587335000000, line ~1321). Wm/2 would also be inconsistent with the page's own need for s/W to be close to m (so that tau is close to 1).

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls
note: Cited, but the page does not say which bound or how it follows: the bound is s<WD, i.e. the number of calls per network is less than the full WD, giving the saving of a power. The content and role of the cited claim are unstated.

quote: Each unit of rank costs one smaller call. (cited)
note: The page never says what a smaller call is or why a unit of matrix rank on an edge costs one such call (in the paper, the edge change is implemented by one smaller interchange per unit of rational rank, via the tape shear). The cited claim stands in for how the construction's cost works and is not explained.

quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation
note: Wrong. The three updates are address maps on the fields H, D (residue arithmetic mod q^b), each an exact permutation of array entries; they are not XORs of the values D and H, so 'after the first update D holds the XOR of D and H' is false. The XOR combinations of data arise inside the bit network (pointwise XOR gates on role streams) that implements the middle shear (paper lines 441, 1129-1131, 2575). The explanation of why the exact permutation survives intermediate XORs is therefore not what the page says.

quote: Signed label changes telescope along each wire, and gate labels cancel.
note: The page never says that every wire touching a gate has the same label before and after it (one common label per gate), nor what the gate labels are, so the reader cannot see why the sum cancels.

quote: each combining $D$ with the earlier field $H$ in linear time
note: The page gives no reason these updates take O(V) tape time when H and D are far apart with spectator fields between them. The paper gets it from Lemma ordered-affine-streams (a later field updated from earlier fields, line 556 and line 1357), which the page never states, so this reader cannot check the claim.

quote: each of its $s$ smaller calls acts on one role stream of volume $V/W$
note: Missing hypothesis. The paper (Proposition power-interchange, lines ~1486-1487 and the proof at ~1500-1510) obtains W role streams of volume V/W only by splitting whole rows cyclically, and requires a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k (rows are padded in Lemma chunk-swap, lines ~1672-1690). The page never mentions rows or this divisibility condition, and it states the V/W reduction and the final O(Vu^tau) bound for all arrays without it.

quote: Every rational $M$ factors as $M=F_1\Pi F_2$, where $F_1$ and $F_2$ are lower-triangular rational matrices.
note: The page then uses F_1^{-1} and F_2^{-1}, which exist only if the factors are invertible, but lower-triangular alone does not give that (a zero diagonal entry is allowed). Paper Lemma lower-lower (line 1364-1371) requires E_1,E_2 to be invertible lower triangular.

quote: by a restoration device the paper introduces as new
note: Misattributed. The paper (lines 354-360, 708-710) says its scratch schedule is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation of Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff and Speelman, Section 3, not a new device. Also, Lemma scalar-motifs gives (X,Y) -> (-Y,X), which is the exchange only in the bit construction.

quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator
note: The page never says what a source, gate, sink, node, edge or route of the network is (a wire's first vertex, a linear map on several wires, its last vertex, a segment between consecutive vertices). The reader has only 'a fixed wiring of linear steps'.

The chain says exp(-2^{-50} ln mu) < 1-20*2^{-50}, which is the wrong direction and is false (exp(-x) > 1-x, and ln mu < 20 gives exp(-2^{-50} ln mu) > exp(-20*2^{-50}) > 1-20*2^{-50}). The paper (lines 1334-1336) has m^{1-2^{-50}} = m exp(...) > m(1-20*2^{-50}) > m(1-eta). The chain with < then > also proves nothing about mu^{-2^{-50}} versus 1-eta; it should read > 1-20*2^{-50} > 1-eta.

quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk
note: Kernel is never defined on the page or in the reader's known concepts. In the paper it is the individual selected-bit C kernel (a 2x2 butterfly on one address bit), costing O(V) per kernel; the reader cannot see why the leaf cost is O(f/m^nu).

quote: as in Alon's construction that the paper specializes
note: The paper (line 872-875) says it specializes Alon's construction to the prime 2 'with the ground-set size changed to h=100'; h=100 is the paper's own choice, not Alon's. The page states it as if Alon's construction used h=100.

quote: $N$ the number of negative source projections
note: Wires, source projections, decreasing edges and dimension changes belong to the construction of the bit network; the page gives no definition and the linked page does not supply them here, so the reader cannot tell what N or L_b count.

quote: Each of the $3\binom h3^2$ invocations has $h$ central wires, each losing $h$ on a decreasing edge, so $L=3\binom h3^2h^2$.
note: The page never defines invocations (three stages, each of binom(h,3)^2 independent invocations), central wires, or which edge loses dimension h and why no other edge decreases (paper's lemma, lines 1000-1010 and 1117-ish 'L=Ich').

quote: for the bit procedure this ring is $\mathbb F_2$, where subtraction and addition coincide
note: Wrong ring. The paper's shear (H,D) -> (H+D,D) acts on address fields over Z/q^b Z for a fixed odd prime q (Lemma matrix-shear, paper.tex lines 1395-1404; Proposition power-interchange, lines 1481-1483, uses radix-q digits). The F_2 scalars (line 689) are the data bits of the XOR network, not the address ring. With q odd, subtraction and addition do not coincide, so the three updates are not XORs and the page's F_2 example does not describe the construction.

quote: The geometric sum is also $O(m^{k\tau})$, since it is $O((s/W)^k)$.
note: Not justified as stated: sum_{j<k}(s/W)^j is O((s/W)^k) only if s/W > 1; if s/W <= 1 the sum is at most k+1 (or bounded), which is not O((s/W)^k). The paper (about line 1556) splits the cases: a<=1 gives at most k+1 = O(m^{k tau}); a>1 gives O(a^k). The page gives neither case split, and its 'since m>=2' is never established on the page.

quote: Along a side wire, a label containing $t_T$ may grow to $t_S^\perp$, since $t_T\perp t_S$, adding $h-2$ dimensions.
note: Labels are subspaces of F=(Q^h)^{tensor 3}, but t_S^perp lies in Q^h and t_T is not a label of F; the paper (lines 945-955, 1048-1055) applies this only to the P tensor factor (P x <t_X> inside P x t_Y^perp), with other factors suppressed. The page gives no assignment of labels to the gates, so the reader cannot see how this relates to the labels U_iota.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: This does not follow from 'q must not divide xi' for each entry being read; it is a separate choice of q. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, around line 1415-1420) picks q odd avoiding every denominator in the table of factors and inverses and the numerators of the diagonal entries of the invertible factors (for example q larger than all nonzero numerators and denominators), done once independent of b. The page never says how such a fixed q is found or why it makes the factors invertible mod q^b.

quote: If $\lambda\le1$ the sum is at most $d$.
note: The sum 1+lambda+...+lambda^d has d+1 terms, each at most 1, so it is at most d+1, not d (at lambda=1 it equals d+1 > d). The paper (paper.tex lines 1555-1556) says 'at most k+1'. The conclusion O(mu^{d tau}) still holds, but the stated bound is wrong.

quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
note: Does not follow: with f>=d^vartheta one only gets f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} <= f, and for f near d^vartheta the factor d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is about f^{1-sigma}, which exceeds f^{lambda-sigma} since lambda<1. So the bound is not O(f^lambda). The paper (lines 2421-2442) keeps the leaf bound as O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and only afterwards combines pieces into O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda'>sigma+beta(1-sigma).

quote: gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}R-N+2L_{\rm b}$
note: The identity is stated with no derivation and the page does not say how edge ranks relate to dimension changes, why each negative source projection contributes as it does, or what labels and edge matrices the bit network has. The reader cannot check it from the page; the paper derives it in Proposition bit-motif-interface (line 1139) from Lemma motif-residuals.

quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
note: The page does not say what a row addition is or why the node's outside work (changes of basis, gates, corrections) is a fixed number of them. Its stated cost O(V(u^tau+1)) is not derived from the interchange cost O(Vu^tau) given just before; it comes from a separate lemma of the paper (lines 2004-2010, 2226) with extra hypotheses.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls
note: The cited claim is not stated: the page does not say what the bound is (the paper: s<Wm) or how it follows from the derived s<WD, so its content and role are unclear.

quote: By the telescoping, the route applies
note: The reader is not told why the route operator has the source frame inverse applied: the page never says that the supplied physical input f is read as the logical array D_in^{-1} f (paper lines 141-142, 797-798), so the stored array at the source is f and not D_source(w) f. Without this the telescoped product is not the operator applied to the supplied input.

quote: which only the paper's later division algorithm needs, not its main multiplication theorem
note: False. The recursion with exponent lambda<1 and the resulting d^{lambda'} layer bound are used in the main multiplication algorithm: the paper's introduction says the cost O(V d^{lambda'}) is for 'the layouts used in the multiplication algorithm' (lines 93-99), the power saving gives the O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) bound of Theorem 1 (line 386, section at line 2393), and the exponents tau, sigma, lambda, lambda' are fixed for the multiplication proof (line 4010). The division section (line 4996) only reuses them.

quote: each combining $D$ with $H$, which lies after $D$ on the tape, in linear time
note: Wrong order. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, line ~1397: 'every H_i before every D_j'; line ~1518: 'The other two updates target the later group and have linear cost'; line ~1432: 'target a later field controlled by an earlier field') has H before D on the tape. The two linear-cost updates change the later field D using the earlier field H, which is what makes them linear-time. The page's 'after' contradicts the shear convention and breaks the stated reason for linear cost.

quote: The paper cites this factorization from earlier work without proof
note: Inconsistent with the paper: Lemma lower-lower (lines 1364-1392) states the factorization and gives its elementary elimination proof; Grigor'ev is credited only for the Bruhat factorization it is adapted from (line 1360-1362). The paper proves it, not merely cites it.

quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
note: Inequality direction is wrong. From s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, s_b < W_b R requires N > 2L_b; N < 2L_b would give s_b > W_b R. The paper says 'Its deficit from W_b m is N-2L_b>0' (line 1176), so N > 2L_b.

The page never gives the matrix size mu of the explicit network, so the reader cannot check mu<2^20. The paper has m=h^3=1000000 (line 656), which is below 2^20. The step ln mu<20 also uses ln 2<1, which is not said.

quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through
note: Inconsistent with the page's own formula: a route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, so with source frame I and sink frame D_nu the operator is eps_w D_nu, equal to D_nu only when the sign is +1.

quote: So the shear needs $\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}M$ interchanges plus $O(V)$ further work.
note: The paper's Lemma matrix-shear (line 1394) assumes every H field comes before every D field in tape order, which is what makes D_tau <- D_tau + H_sigma an update of a later field by an earlier one, doable in linear time. The page omits this layout hypothesis and the O(V) bound for the two additions is not justified without it.

quote: Each of the $2\binom h3^2$ invocations
note: Wrong count and inconsistent with the page's own result: with 2*binom(h,3)^2 invocations, each having h central wires losing h, the loss would be 2*binom(h,3)^2*h^2, not the stated L=3*binom(h,3)^2*h^2 (which is what gives 100/539). The paper (line 676) has I=3v^2 invocations, v=binom(h,3): three stages, v^2 invocations each; L=Ich (line 1003). The page also never says where the invocations come from.

quote: Over $\mathbb F_2$ each update is a pointwise XOR, since addition and subtraction are the same operation
note: The three updates are address permutations (entry at address (H,D) moves to (H+D,D)) over Z/q^b Z, not XORs of data values; the XOR gates act on the data in the network, and the page's claim that 'D holds the XOR of D and H' mixes the two. In the paper the field updates are not XORs of data and the intermediate XOR combinations belong to the gate network (line 441).

quote: Each smaller call acts on one of the $W$ [wire streams](role-streams.md), each of volume $V/W$.
note: The split into W streams of volume V/W, repeated at every depth, needs a row field preceding both chunks whose length is divisible by W^k (Proposition power-interchange, paper.tex lines 1481-1485). The page states no such hypothesis and presents the recursion for any array, so the recursion analysis is missing a hypothesis. The paper removes it by padding in the arbitrary-width lemma (lines 1631-1735), which the page does not mention.

quote: $$\Phi(mf)\le\frac{s}{W}\Phi(f)-C(mf)^\lambda.$$
note: The outside work must be added, not subtracted: the paper's recurrence is F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1) (paper.tex, Unrolling the recurrence, around line 2380). With a minus sign the bound is not the cost recurrence, and it contradicts the later sum of positive internal costs C f^lambda sum (...)^nu.

quote: for the bit procedure this ring is $\mathbb F_2$, where subtraction and addition coincide
note: Does not match the paper. The address fields H, D are vectors of radix-q digit fields over Z/q^b Z for a fixed odd prime q (Lemma matrix-shear, paper lines 1395-1410; Proposition power-interchange, line 1479; the factorization needs q to avoid denominators). The paper (line 148) says only 'a common residue ring'. F_2 is the scalar ring of the data gates, not the ring of address fields, and in Z/q^b Z with q odd subtraction and addition do not coincide. The same error is in the 'shear ... over F_2' sentence.

quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
note: Does not follow from 'q must not divide xi', which only constrains denominators. The paper (lines 1411-1415) avoids every denominator and the numerators of diagonal entries of invertible factors (e.g. a prime exceeding all nonzero numerators and denominators); a zero numerator is divisible by every q.

quote: The first edge out of each source has matrix $2P_{U_\iota}$, rank one, with no label change
note: The page does not say that the first gate on the source's wire has label exactly U_iota (true at stage 1 where B=0), which is what makes the edge matrix P_U-(-P_U)=2P_U with no label change; the reader cannot check it.

quote: Since $\vartheta=\tfrac12$ is a fixed exponent, $d\le f^{1/\vartheta}$
note: Being a fixed exponent does not give this inequality. It holds only at internal nodes, where f >= d^vartheta (paper line 2413), and that stopping rule is introduced only in the next paragraph. The hypothesis is missing at the point of use.

quote: carries a linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set
note: The page uses D_alpha^{-1} and D_source^{-1} but never states that frames are invertible (paper line 133 and 793: invertible linear operator), nor that all incidences of one gate use the same frame; the commuting identity and the edge operator need both.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: The sentence does not state the property: the bound it refers to (s < W m, from 2L < N) and its role in the recursion are never said.

quote: The paper's decisive property is a bound on the number of smaller calls, (cited).
note: A cited result whose content and role the page does not state: it gives no bound, does not say what a smaller call is, and does not say how s<WD yields the recursive saving.

quote: For every linear network, $s<Wm$ (cited)
note: Stated far too widely. In the paper (lines 1458-1468, and 168) s<Wm is a contract condition (eq. finite-shear-contract) that the specific constructed three-element-subset network is shown to satisfy, with s=Wm minus a positive deficit. It is not true of every linear network, whose rank sum can exceed Wm. The page should say 'for the network constructed in the paper'.

quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
note: The page asserts that the outside work (changes of basis, scalar gates, corrections, reassembly) reduces to a fixed number of row additions and that a row addition costs O(V(u^tau+1)), but it only cites the cost of an interchange. Neither why the count is fixed nor why a row addition has the same cost is given (the paper derives these at lines 2268-2290 from the fixed network and a separate lemma).

quote: Both are $O(m^{k\tau})$, since $m\ge2$.
note: Bounding the sum by k (case s/W<=1) as O(m^{k tau}) needs m^tau>1, i.e. tau>0, not just m>=2; the page only says to fix tau<1 with s/W<m^tau, which a nonpositive tau could satisfy when s/W is small. The paper chooses tau in (0,1) (Proposition power-interchange, line 1481). The page also never states m>=2 (paper line 1451).
